rules.problem: The 'lower leg or foot' site pair omits the ankle: 'Ankle region structure' is not a descendant of 'Structure of lower limb from knee to ankle' nor of 'Foot structure' (it sits under 'Structure of ankle and/or foot'), so an ambulant patient's ankle ulcer (the classic venous site, and one of the eight pressure sites the same task checks) never satisfies 'Is ulcer on the lower leg or foot?'. Add (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Skin ulcer" "disorder") (finding_site (snomed_concept "Ankle region structure" "body structure"))) to the lower-leg/foot group here and in the three site-based diagnosis rules. Also, the page's identify-cause flow starts from 'skin ulcer or non-healing wound' but every site finding is 'Skin ulcer' only, so a non-healing wound on the leg can never reach arterial, venous or diabetic ulcer.

The pulse measurement uses 'Pulse, function', a function observable rather than a rate; 'Heart rate' (observable entity) is the rate concept unless the house records pulse under another name.

rules.rule: Urgent: skin ulcer or non-healing wound with critical limb ischaemia
rules.problem: Urgent via (active_condition Critical lower limb ischemia) is the briefing's pattern for a red-box 'X likely'.

summary: Nothing is invented and no number, direction or unit is wrong; the red box, the eight pressure sites and the four 'likely' diagnoses are all on the page. The most consequential problem is structural: 'Is ulcer on the lower leg or foot?' is encoded as knee-to-ankle OR foot, and SNOMED puts 'Ankle region structure' under neither, so an ambulant patient's ankle ulcer (the classic venous site) can never reach the arterial, venous or diabetic rules; the same rules also accept only 'Skin ulcer', dropping the non-healing-wound presentation the page routes through the same flow. Lesser points: 'Pulse, function' is a function observable rather than a rate concept ('Heart rate' exists), 'Acute confusion' is narrower than 'confused', and the site-less 'Hyperpigmentation of skin' is broader than 'darkening of skin around ulcer'.
